top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn; B001) is the only proposal on the slate. It rewards a mature, original measurement advance: estimating demand with endogenous prices and heterogeneous substitution, plus the dynamic-industry framework. It made merger, markup and welfare counterfactuals possible that earlier reduced-form work could not. It has about thirty years of use in regulatory practice and has spread into trade, health and environmental economics. Its main sensitivities (numerics, instruments, functional form) have been studied over that period. Attribution is comparatively clean: the 1995 paper is jointly authored by the three named laureates, so the citation does not split a single result. The costs are real. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are left out, the toolkit-versus-discovery weighting is a judgement, and Pakes's dynamic-games and production-function work is only partly claimed. I judge these costs acceptable under a method-level citation, and the prize is clearly preferable to no award. This rests on background knowledge and the round-2 exchange, not on independently verified citation or adoption data.
recusal_note: No tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent from the profile. Disclosed, not adjudicated: frequent co-authorship with Timo Boppart and John Hassler, and IIES colleagueship with both, who are committee colleagues and not candidates. My field of heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics is not adjacent to B001.
